As expected, the PUE also went down with ambient temperature (T ) at 3.7 and amb 2.5 kW; however, the reduction in PUE was again limited by the minimum fan speed (23%) and pump speed (35%). The results also show that PUE is lower at higher loads since the system power consumption increases at a lower rate with the same relative increase in thermal load. This is desirable given that at higher loads more fan and pump power are required. In other words, there is greater impact of PUE at higher loads. These results show that very low PUE values are achievable using this technology. At a load of 5 kW, near the tank’s design load of 6 kW, the highest PUE was only 1.07 at a relatively warm ambient temperature of 35°C. At 17°C, the PUE is only 1.03 with possible further reduction if the minimum fan speed can be further reduced. One can also notice that there is little change of PUE for temperatures below 27 °C. In fact, the difference of PUE is within uncertainty for temperatures between 27°C and 17°C. This indicates that even in warmer US locations such as Florida, with an average annual temperature of about 23 °C, the measured PUE for this equipment would be very low. 9 For comparison, the average PUE of a US data center was about 1.5 in 2021 [22]. Improved PUEs can be achieved with 2PIC primarily because of its operation at higher coolant temperatures than air-cooled systems. A typical air-cooled data center will require facility coolant temperatures of about 5 °C–15 °C; while for this test, cooling near the maximum thermal load was possible at coolant temperatures above 40°C. Because of lower coolant temperatures, many of the air-cooled data centers might also require evaporative cooling and consume significant amounts of water, whereas coolant temperatures near 40 °C can help significantly reduce water use.
